# HyMarkX (HMX)

> A Markdown-compatible language that compiles documents to HTML, and progressively to
> styled, component-based, interactive pages. Ordinary Markdown is already valid HMX.
> Static documents emit zero JavaScript; interactivity costs about 1 KB.

Alpha. Phases 0–8 of 10 complete. Published to npm as `hymarkx`; syntax may still change.

**If you are generating or editing `.hmx` files, read "Rules that prevent the common
mistakes" below. Most errors come from four things, all listed there.**

## Rules that prevent the common mistakes

These are the failures actually observed while building the language — including one that
shipped in this project's own README for six phases.

**1. Nesting containers needs MORE colons on the outer fence.**

```md
::::grid{columns=2}

:::card
Inner
:::

::::
```

`:::grid` wrapping `:::card` at the same width does **not** nest — the inner fence closes
the outer container and you get `HMX1001`. This is the single most common mistake.

**2. Interpolation is `{{ expr }}`, never `{ expr }`.**

Single braces are ordinary text (they appear in 4 CommonMark conformance examples).
Attribute *values* use single braces: `{title={site.name}}`.

**3. `@state`, `@if`, `@for` do not exist.** They appear in early design sketches and were
formally rejected in ADR-0014. Everything is a directive. State is `::state{count=0}`.

**4. Expressions cannot call functions.** No `toUpperCase()`, no `Math.max()`, no
`fetch()`. Identifiers not in scope are compile errors, not `undefined`. Assignment is legal
**only** inside an event handler, and only to declared state.

## Syntax

```md
---
title: Dashboard          # frontmatter: metadata, and the scope for {{ }}
---

# {{ title }}             # interpolation, resolved at compile time

:::note[Heads up]{type=warning}   # container directive: name, [label], {attributes}
Body content.
:::

::children                # leaf directive (inside component files only)

:badge[live]{kind=success}   # text directive, inline

::state{count=0}          # reactive state, component-local

:::button{on-click="count = count + 1"}
Increment
:::
```

Attributes: `{key=value}`, `{key="quoted value"}`, `{flag}` (bare, means true), `{#id}`,
`{.class}`. Shorthands may be mixed with named attributes in any order.

## Built-in components

| Name | Form | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| `note` | container | `type`: info \| warning \| danger \| success (default info) |
| `card` | container | — |
| `box` | container | `as`: div \| section \| article \| nav \| header \| footer \| aside \| main (default div) — no class, no CSS; use it for layout wrappers and page landmarks |
| `grid` | container | `columns`: number (default 3), `gap`: number (default 4) |
| `metric` | container | — |
| `badge` | text | `kind`: info \| warning \| danger \| success (default info) |
| `button` | container | `type`: button \| submit \| reset (default button) |
| `input` | leaf or container | `type`: text, `value`: string, `name`: string |
| `form` | container | — |

`id`, `class`, and `title` are accepted on every component without being declared. If a
component's schema declares one of those names, it becomes that component's prop and is no
longer also emitted as an HTML attribute — `class` and `id` are the exceptions and always merge.

## Authoring a reusable component

A component is a `.hmx` file in `components/`, named with a capital letter. Props are
declared in frontmatter using the same schema shape as built-ins.

```md
---
props:
  title: { type: string, required: true }
  tone: { type: enum, values: [info, warning], default: info }
---

:::note{type={tone}}
## {{ title }}

::children
:::
```

Used as `:::Card{title="Revenue"}`. Capitalised names are yours; lowercase are built-in.
A component's props are its **entire** scope — it cannot see the caller's frontmatter.

## What does not exist yet

Do not generate these; they are recorded decisions, not oversights:

- named derived state (`::derived`) — deferred, ADR-0014
- shared or global state between components — no ambient store by design
- named slots — only the default `::children`
- `async`, data loading, `fetch`, effects, lifecycle hooks
- TSX interop — Phase 8, not started
- author `<style>` in `document` trust mode — `app` mode only
- loops or conditionals of any kind — there is no `if` or `for`

## Trust modes

`document` (default) rejects `<script>`, `<style>`, and raw HTML outside an allowlist, and
restricts URL schemes. `app` permits them. **The host chooses the mode; no document
construct can change it.** Interactivity works in both, because expressions cannot reach a
host object.

## Toolchain

```bash
hmx build page.hmx --out dist   # compile
hmx check page.hmx              # diagnostics only
hmx fmt page.hmx --check        # formatting, CI mode
hmx dev .                       # dev server with live reload
```

Diagnostics have stable codes: `HMX1xxx` syntax, `HMX2xxx` semantic, `HMX3xxx` security,
`HMX4xxx` accessibility, `HMX5xxx` configuration and I/O. `hmx check` is the fastest way to
verify generated output — if it exits 0, the document is valid.
